name: Linked lists
tagline: Rewire the arrows in place. Save next before you cut.

blocks.html:
A treasure hunt: each clue only tells you where the next one is. You cannot jump to clue 5; you follow the chain.

So linked list tricks use two pointers, or rewire next in place, instead of copying into an array.

blocks.code:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, val):
        self.val, self.next = val, None

def build(vals, loop_to):          # tail points back to index loop_to, or -1 for none
    nodes = [Node(v) for v in vals]
    for a, b in zip(nodes, nodes[1:]):
        a.next = b
    if loop_to >= 0:
        nodes[-1].next = nodes[loop_to]
    return nodes[0]

def slow(head):                    # brute force: remember every node in a list, O(N^2)
    seen = []
    while head:
        if head in seen:           # list scan, O(N) each time
            return True
        seen.append(head)
        head = head.next
    return False

def fast(head):                    # Floyd: two speeds, O(N) time, O(1) space
    walker = runner = head
    while runner and runner.next:
        walker = walker.next
        runner = runner.next.next
        if walker is runner:       # runner lapped walker
            return True
    return False

for vals, loop_to in [([1, 2, 3, 4], 1), ([1, 2, 3], -1), ([7], 0)]:
    head = build(vals, loop_to)
    print(slow(head), fast(head))  # -> True True, then False False, then True True
blocks.note: Remember every node, then two pointers at two speeds

blocks.html: Two pointers, one twice as fast. In a loop the fast one must catch the slow one; without a loop it hits None first. No extra memory needed.

options: It finds where the cycle starts
blocks.why: Without a cycle, runner reaches the end. None.next raises AttributeError.

pitfalls: Save cur.next before you overwrite it, or you lose the rest of the list.
Use a dummy head node when the first node can change (merge, delete). It removes the special case.
Compare nodes with is, not by value: two nodes can hold the same value.
